dublinCore.title: Citation Graph for FFT on Microcontrollers
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
FFT
Embedded Systems
Citation Analysis
Academic Research
dublinCore.description: Interactive citation graph of 15 sample papers about running the FFT on microcontrollers and embedded hardware, with filters by research area and citation count and three layouts.

learningObjectives: Explain how a citation network encodes papers as nodes and directed citation relationships as edges
Identify foundational FFT papers by their large node size, since node diameter is scaled to citation count
Distinguish the color-coded research domains in the graph, including foundational, manycore, and FPGA approaches to FFT implementation
Analyze how filtering by research area or minimum citation count changes which clusters remain visible
Evaluate the coverage limits of a 15-paper demonstration dataset relative to a systematic search using the Scopus, OpenAlex, or Semantic Scholar APIs

misconceptions.misconception: A bigger node means a better paper
misconceptions.correction: Node size reflects how often a paper is cited, not its correctness or quality; older papers have had longer to accumulate citations
misconceptions.evidence: Compare the 2022 CORDIC paper (15 citations) with the 1965 Cooley-Tukey paper (5000 citations) in the information panel

misconceptions.misconception: Papers drawn close together are more similar
misconceptions.correction: Only arrows and colors carry information; positions in the physics layout are arbitrary for papers that are not linked
misconceptions.evidence: Switch the layout to Circular and the same papers are spaced evenly with no change in meaning

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Interactive directed citation graph of 15 papers about FFT implementations on microcontrollers. Each node is a paper, sized by citation count and colored by research area. Each arrow points from the citing paper to the cited paper. Click a node to read its details. Controls filter by research area and minimum citation count and switch the layout.

controls.label: Filter by Group
controls.description: Shows only the papers of one research area; links to hidden papers are hidden too

controls.label: Min Citations
controls.description: Hides papers whose citation count is below the slider value

controls.label: Layout
controls.description: Chooses how the nodes are positioned: physics simulation, hierarchical levels or a circle

controls.label: Reset View
controls.description: Restores All Groups, Min Citations 0 and the Physics layout, closes the information panel and fits the graph in view

controls.label: Export Data
controls.description: Downloads the visible papers and links as a JSON file

visualElements.description: Directed citation network: nodes are papers sized by citation count and colored by research area, arrows point from the citing paper to the cited paper
Information panel with authors, year, venue, citation count, abstract and citation connections of the clicked paper
Legend of research-area colors and a statistics line with paper, link and research-area counts and the average citation count

model.description: Directed graph of 15 papers and 25 citation links from an embedded sample data set; node positions come from a force-directed simulation, a hierarchical layout or a circle
algorithms: ForceAtlas2-based force-directed layout (vis physics, fixed random seed)
assumptions: Each link is a citation from the first paper to the second paper
limitations: Citation counts and links are illustrative and not verified against a citation database
Only 15 papers; a systematic search would return many more

instructionalStrategies: Find the hub paper, then predict what each filter will leave visible before applying it
Compare the same graph in three layouts
Plan a systematic literature search as a follow-up
extensions: Replace the sample data with a graph built from OpenAlex or Semantic Scholar
Add centrality metrics or publication-year coloring
